confirmed: Read the complete markdown and all 10 PDF pages, including the references; the document is the published Proceedings of the Design Society, Volume 5: ICED25 paper, printed pp. 479-488, with the title and authors recorded in the form (PDF p. 1, header/title/authors; PDF p. 10, references/footer).

The human operators are the authors, and five concept-creation approaches are applied sequentially to AI-agents. No randomized people study or human assistance-group comparison is reported; model_only, core no, and context_class none are supported (PDF pp. 3-4, printed pp. 481-482, section 3 and Table 1).

Participant randomized and analyzed counts appropriately remain null: the illustrative case reports 50 ideas per AI-agent and 150 ideas across three AI-agents, not people. There is no reported human participant analysis to classify as an experiment below the 50-person threshold (PDF p. 3, section 3, human operators; PDF p. 6, printed p. 484, section 4).

The models are ChatGPT-4o, ChatGPT-o1, and Gemini Advanced; the design cases have known patented control solutions, with the twist-off screw cap as the detailed illustration. The total number of design cases is not stated (PDF p. 3, printed p. 481, section 3; PDF p. 8, section 5).

The five approach descriptions match Table 1, including human-selected core ideas supplemented with AI-selected complementary ideas in Approach 4 and five AI-selected solution principles in Approach 5 (PDF p. 4, printed p. 482, Table 1).

Total Value combines automated usefulness, feasibility, complexity, and novelty ratings; the paper presents AI self-evaluations and cross-evaluations, not human participant creativity scores (PDF p. 5, Table 2; PDF p. 7, Table 6; PDF p. 8, printed p. 486, equation (1)).

S1-O1 reported and the one-line finding are numerically correct: Approach 4 has the highest average Total Value, 4.20, and Approach 1 the lowest, 3.80 (PDF p. 9, printed p. 487, section 5, first paragraph).

S1-O2 reported is correct: Approaches 2 and 5 jointly account for nearly 60% of the strongest concepts; Approach 3 contributes approximately 22%. These are concept shares, not participant percentages (PDF p. 8, printed p. 486, section 5, final paragraph).

The approach-level averages and strongest-concept shares have no reported denominators or uncertainty estimates; example-level production counts do not establish those denominators. The form correctly avoids assigning them participant or total analyzed-output counts (PDF pp. 6-9, sections 4-5, especially the aggregate results on pp. 8-9).

This is an original workflow study, not a synthesis; no pooled estimates are reported. No appendix is included and no supplementary material is identified in the complete document (PDF pp. 1-10; methods in section 3 and references on PDF p. 10).
summary: The complete proceedings paper supports the model-only classification and contains no randomized human-participant study. Both reported findings match the PDF, and the form correctly leaves participant counts null because the reported counts concern AI-generated ideas and concepts.
